cards.example: Mi ha salutato con un ciao.
cards.note: Said "chow"; the i only signals that the c is soft like ch. Use ciao with people you know and buongiorno with strangers.
Said GRAHT-syeh, and the final e is clearly pronounced. Grazie mille means a thousand thanks.
Prego is an all-rounder: you're welcome, here you go, come in. To ask for something, say per favore instead.

cards.example: Ti chiedo scusa per il ritardo.
cards.note: Say scusa to friends and the polite scusi to strangers. The sc before u sounds like sk: SKOO-za.
With the accent, sì means yes; without it, si is a pronoun (oneself). Both sound the same.
cq sounds like a long kw: AHK-kwah. In a restaurant you choose naturale (still) or frizzante (sparkling).
Italian vowels are always full: PAH-neh, and the final e is spoken. Don't mix it up with la panna, which is cream.

cards.example: Marco è l'amico di mio fratello.
cards.note: The plural of amico is amici, said ah-MEE-chee. The c before i sounds like ch.
gi sounds like j, and the i isn't spoken separately: mahn-JAH-reh.
Short and clear: BEH-reh, with one tap of the r. I drink is irregular: io bevo.
Roll the r with the tip of your tongue. Parla inglese? politely asks whether someone speaks English.
Double consonants are held longer: OHD-jee. The gi sounds like j.
Stress the middle syllable: doh-MAH-nee. A domani means see you tomorrow.
Two syllables: YEH-ree, the first i sounds like y. Ieri sera means last night.
Before masculine nouns it often shortens to buon: buon giorno. For the adverb, as in I'm fine, use bene.
False friend: largo means wide, not large. Said GRAHN-deh, with a full e at the end.
The double c is a long k: PEEK-koh-loh. A piccolo is simply the small flute.
Hold the double l: BEHL-loh. Before nouns it often shortens to bel: un bel giorno.
Caro also means dear, as at the start of a letter: Caro Luca. Tap the r once.
Stress the third syllable: eh-koh-NOH-mee-koh. You'll also hear a buon mercato.
Two syllables: DOH-veh. Before è it usually shortens to dov'è: Dov'è il bagno?
qu sounds like kw: KWAHN-toh. The ending adapts: quanti giorni, quante ore.
zi sounds like tsy: stah-TSYOH-neh. The main station is often called stazione centrale.

cards.example: Ci porta il conto, per favore?
cards.note: Conto also means bank account. Il conto, per favore! is the standard line in a restaurant.
Many Italians have breakfast standing at a bar, with a cappuccino and a cornetto. Said koh-lah-TSYOH-neh.
False friend: camera means room; a camera is la macchina fotografica. Stress the first syllable: KAH-meh-rah.
Stress: lah-voh-RAH-reh. Don't confuse it with lavare, to wash.

cards.example: Non riesco a capire questa parola.
cards.note: Non capisco is one of the most useful sentences. In the present tense the verb adds -isc-: capisco, capisci.
Come stai is for friends, come sta for strangers. The answer: bene, grazie!

cards.example: Se n'è andato senza dire arrivederci.
cards.note: Literally "until we see each other again". Said ahr-ree-veh-DEHR-chee, with a strongly rolled double r.
